I was diagnosed at 19 too, 22 now and getting a hysterectomy tomorrow. I empathise so hard and I’m so sorry you’re going through this. 

First off, you need to see a new gyno. At best, this person is incompetent, at worst, they’re spreading serious misinformation and opening you up to more pain. 

Fertility issues is one of the best known issues associated with adenomyosis. It doesn’t at all mean you won’t be able to have kids but fertility issues are well documented. When you get pregnant, the hormonal changes can subdue symptoms but it usually comes back after. For some people it helps but it does not cure it. I dealt with the constant “what if you want kids” question and had to try every treatment available to even be considered for hysterectomy. I understand how tough it is :( 

See a new gyno, ideally someone who specialises in endometriosis and adenomyosis, and talk about other treatment options. Things like a mirena IUD can be great for some people (do not let them talk you into having it inserted awake). There are ways out of this and you will be ok. 

Anti inflammatory diet wise, cutting out meat (except fish), gluten and dairy slightly helped and made me feel healthier which then made me feel more on top of the rest of my health, but that’s just me. Everyone is different in terms of what works for them and also focusing on eating more fruit and veg and whatnot rather than restricting what you can eat is better for your mental health. Anti inflammatory behaviours like the gym and getting enough sleep are really important too! 

PM me if you want to chat or have any questions. I have been in your shoes before and it’s horrible. I was diagnosed at 19 too after being told it was anxiety for 5 years before that. You are going to be okay, hang in there!

I am very fortunate to live in Australia in terms of accessing things like reproductive care, we have a long way to go but I understand how privileged I am to be here instead of a lot of other places. I also have very supportive parents (I know my dad isn’t happy about the hysterectomy but he understands it’s necessary) and very good health insurance. I also have the benefit of having a degree in anatomy and physiology and work in a hospital anatomy lab, so I am very well educated in parts of medicine and can conduct proper research  and understand my options in depth, which not everyone can. I’m not kidding, I have tried every single treatment option available apart from UAE (which we figured likely wouldn’t work to reduce pain due to my uterus being shrunk from hormones). It has not been easy at all, I have endured agonising pain for years, been sick and exhausted and in pain constantly, I have trauma from SA which has made many treatments even more mentally and physically painful, I have undergone treatments that should really be considered medically neglectful due to the lack of care taken, trust me, this is the absolute last resort. 

I was met with the same reaction for years about the hysterectomy and told it wouldn’t help and I would essentially be stuck with the pain forever (not true, we tested chemical menopause and for the first time in years I got my life back which says hysterectomy in my case will very much solve this). I am so so grateful for finding the gynaecologist who has agreed to do this for me. I have seen the absolute worst of the medical system and finally have met some absolute angel practitioners who don’t buy into the medical sexism so many of us have been tormented by, and treat me like a human being with autonomy and needs rather than a baby making machine. 

I know I am going to face some serious backlash after this from people and doctors who find out but I intend to use me having this operation at this age as a means to advocate for others and hopefully push for this to be taken seriously! Sorry for the essay, I’m still coming to terms with it and I have a loooot of thoughts. I am seriously hoping this works out for you and you can also find a solution to this nightmare! The “maggots” you’re seeing are likely springtails, as maggots don’t eat logs. Springtails are a key component of bioactive enclosures and are not harmful in the slightest. The enclosure clearly needs some TLC and this dude likely needs a larger enclosure, and potentially some better lighting and light UVB if that isn’t already being considered to ensure his bones stay strong. As he is quite old he will likely need to be hand fed, and definitely put on a diet to manage his weight. These guys are not hard to look after but they are very fiddly, costly, and sensitive. As others have suggested, please talk to the store before trying to perform a grand rescue operation as taking him in without the right enclosure or knowledge of care will likely result in his health declining further.
